messages:
ash_support: Heads-up — Kestrel (enterprise) is flagging that objects marked for deletion are still showing up in their evidence export. They requested a preservation export yesterday and claim ~120 items should be purged by now. :thinking:
lee_ops: Can you paste the customer ID and the export job id?
ash_support: cust_kestrel_42, export job `exp-2026-03-16-21` — created 2026-03-16T21:03:12Z. They say many items were HSM-encrypted and should have been tombstoned after TTL 30d ended.
maria_sre: Quick question — are they on default retention or did they have a custom policy?
ash_support: They were on our default 30d soft-delete -> 7d tombstone purge. No custom retention. Legal asked to preserve until handover, but support has a ticket showing purge should've started.
alex_infra: I pulled the deletion queue for cust_kestrel_42 around that job id. Queue shows entries marked DEFERRED with reason `kms:decrypt-failed` starting at 2026-03-15T02:00Z. Looks like HSM returned 403 for a subset.
maria_sre: That matches what KMS alerts showed — transient auth errors to HSM cluster eu-west-2 around 2026-03-15 02:00Z-02:40Z. Some keys flagged `locked_for_rollback`.
ash_support: Customer is pushing back — they need a clean evidence export for compliance. Legal wants an audit log of the retention state for those items + timeline.
legal_jordan: @ash_support please confirm we have the audit logs for key access + retention state for each object. We'll need object IDs and timestamps to produce the export for compliance.
lee_ops: Repro steps I ran (minimal):
```
# list objects in export bundle
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/customers/cust_kestrel_42/exports/exp-2026-03-16-21/objects"
# check object metadata
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/objects/<object_id>"
```
Response for one object: 200 with metadata {"status":"deleted","deleted_at":"2026-02-14T03:01:00Z","tombstone_expires":"2026-02-21T03:01:00Z","encryption":"hsm","key_id":"hsm-eu-3"}
But export included full content for same object (should be inaccessible).
ash_support: Customer attached export file, showing content present for ~27 objects. They also saw `500` when calling the Delete API during the incident window.
maria_sre: From infra: when HSM returned 403 we marked those items DEFERRED to avoid corrupt deletes. That prevents the storage delete job from running until key state normalizes. Means data visible in some read paths until tombstone purge runs.
lee_ops: Actionables: 1) Provide legal with list of object IDs + retention flags 2) Run a targeted re-delete once keys unblocked 3) Provide timeline and audit logs for HSM calls 4) Offer mitigations for customer export (temporary redaction)
alex_infra: I can generate the HSM call audit using internal tool. Query I ran: `internal-audit query --keys hsm-eu-3 --from 2026-03-14 --to 2026-03-16 --event decrypt,lock` produced 62 events with 403 and 2 `locked_for_rollback` transitions.
sre-bot: Incident notice created: INC-2026-0316-42. Assigned to @maria_sre and @alex_infra.
legal_jordan: Please include in the audit: request IDs, HSM response codes, object ids, deletion queue status, and ticket IDs. We'll need this for regulator response.
ash_support: I'm drafting a response to the customer offering a 2-step remediation: immediate targeted re-deletion after keys restored + formal compliance package with logs. Any objections?
maria_sre: Sounds right. Also suggest adding explicit `preserve:true` flag logs so legal can certify we didn't proactively purge during the hold.
lee_ops: Operational note — we should add a safe-fail path: when HSM errors occur during purge, mark objects as `preserved_temp` and surface them to the console so customers see why they are in exports. Prevents confusion.
alex_infra: Will attach the export of audit logs to the ticket once generated. ETA 2 hours. Also pushing a hotfix to label DEFERRED items with `hsm_error_code` in the deletion queue for transparency.
ash_support: Customer update sent: "We're investigating; export contents may include items deferred due to HSM errors. We'll provide logs and a remediation plan within 4 hours." :thumbsup:
legal_jordan: Keep me looped. If the customer requests a formal hold extension, we should get a signed request via legal channel.
lee_ops: Follow-up: after keys normalized at 2026-03-15T03:10Z I triggered re-delete on a sample set -> delete API returned 202 acceptance, background job removed blob references and queued tombstone purge. I'll monitor for residual visible content in exports.
ash_support: Thanks all. I'll close the loop with customer once alex uploads logs.
alex_infra: Logs uploaded to ticket TKT-987654. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/TKT-987654
ash_support: Customer replied: appreciated, will hold legal escalation for now. :relieved:
maria_sre: Postmortem TODO: clarify HSM transient error handling for retention flows and add visibility in console.
lee_ops: Filed follow-up RFC: RFC-2026-045: retention-safe-fail-and-visibility, assigned to infra team.
ash_support: Thread will become part of support ticket. Marking as resolved pending audit upload confirmation.
